topStories.headline: Warriors Show Up for Visitacion Valley Middle School — With Benches, Picnic Tables, and a Pair of Little Libraries
topStories.dek: About 100 Golden State Warriors franchise employees spent a day of community service at Viz Valley on September 15, where coach Steve Kerr made a surprise appearance for students who had been expecting Steph Curry.
topStories.body:
Students at Visitacion Valley Middle School got a notable visitor last week — just not the one the rumor mill had promised. Word spread quickly that Steph Curry was on campus, but it was his coach, Steve Kerr, who walked the grounds, led by principal Maya Baker. Mission Local, which covered the visit on September 15, reported that Kerr was part of a roughly 100-person contingent from the Warriors organization — spanning the Golden State Warriors, the Golden State Valkyries, and the Santa Cruz Warriors — volunteering for the franchise's 14th annual All Hands Helping Hands community service day. Viz Valley was one of three schools selected across the city, with 450 Warriors employees spread across all sites.

At the Visitacion Valley campus, volunteers built benches and picnic tables, cleaned up the courtyard, and assembled two Little Free Libraries stocked with books. The new furniture found an immediate audience: students sat down on the benches almost as soon as they were finished. Principal Baker told Mission Local she hoped her students would leave the day understanding that community service is not a punishment.

The visit has a decade-and-a-half of history behind it. Warriors volunteers had previously built a basketball court at Viz Valley during an earlier community service day in 2010. The school recently completed a separate, grant-funded overhaul of its outdoor space, converting that original court into a multipurpose area — a transformation the volunteers were able to see in full on their return.

Viz Valley serves about 300 students. The Little Free Libraries and new courtyard furniture are permanent additions to the campus.

topStories.headline: Bayview's Air-Quality Blueprint Is Now Open for Public Comment After Tuesday Open House
topStories.dek: The Bay Area Air Quality Management District held its public session on the draft Community Emissions Reduction Plan on September 22; the 238-page document is now posted for written comment from any resident.
topStories.body:
The Bay Area Air Quality Management District held a public open house on Tuesday, September 22, at the Southeast Community Center's Alex Pitcher Pavilion on Evans Street, where residents could review and respond to a draft Community Emissions Reduction Plan for Bayview–Hunters Point and surrounding Southeast San Francisco. The 238-page document was revised as recently as September 14 and is now posted for public review and comment on the Air District's website in English, Spanish, and Chinese, with an executive summary available in Tagalog, Vietnamese, Samoan, and Tongan.

The CERP is being developed under California's Assembly Bill 617, the Community Air Protection Program, which directs focused pollution-reduction efforts toward neighborhoods most disproportionately burdened by poor air quality. Bayview–Hunters Point was nominated for the program in September 2022 by the Marie Harrison Community Foundation and the Bayview Hunters Point Community Advocates. The Air District has worked with a community-based steering committee meeting monthly since early 2024 to shape the plan.

Residents who could not attend Tuesday's session can still submit written comments by emailing Air District senior staff specialist Daniel Madrigal at dmadrigal@baaqmd.gov. Once finalized, the plan is intended to serve as an enforceable blueprint implemented by the Air District, the California Air Resources Board, and community partners — the culmination of more than four years of community organizing and scientific documentation.
topStories.sourceName: Bay Area Air Quality Management District

topStories.headline: Three Nights of Free Music Come to Third Street — With a Latin Concert to Follow at the Ruth
topStories.dek: People's Garden hosts the free 'Night Garden on Third' outdoor music series October 2–4, and the Ruth Williams Opera House presents its fifth annual Afro-Latinx Concert on October 3.
topStories.body:
Bayview's People's Garden at 4101 Third Street will host a free three-night outdoor music series, Night Garden on Third, running Friday, October 2, through Sunday, October 4, from 7 to 9 p.m. each evening. According to Mission Local's Bayview Buzz column published September 23, Bayview native Martin Luther McCoy will host all three nights, which will feature live music from Jazz Mafia and Horns in the Hood alongside vinyl sets by DJ POS Red — moving through afrobeats, jazz, and soul across the three evenings.

The same Saturday — October 3 — the Ruth Williams Bayview Opera House at 4705 Third Street hosts the fifth annual Afro-Latinx Concert. Doors open at 7 p.m. with the show beginning at 7:30 p.m. The all-ages event is hosted by Oakland-based Gina Madrid and features live hip-hop, reggae, and cumbia representing Latin America, the Caribbean, and the Bay Area. Admission is by donation; a pre-show community dinner option is also available.

The Ruth Williams Opera House has served as a cultural anchor in Bayview–Hunters Point since receiving nonprofit status in 1992. This year's Afro-Latinx Concert falls during Latino Heritage Month. Both the Night Garden series and the concert are free or donation-based and open to all ages, making the first weekend of October an unusually full stretch for live music along the Third Street corridor.

Free admission; the street is closed noon to 10 p.m. and the 56 Rutland reroutes around the event.

moreNews.headline: Community-Backed Pharmacy Moves Closer to Opening on Third Street
moreNews.body: More than a year after Bayview–Hunters Point's last Walgreens closed in February 2025 — leaving nearly 35,000 residents without a local pharmacy — a community-led replacement is in the pipeline. The D10 Community Pharmacy, led by Bayview Senior Services' Cathy Davis and Geoffrea Morris (who also run the neighborhood's free D10 Community Market), received a Storefront Opportunity Grant from the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development and is slated to open at 5668 Third St., the former storefront of What's the Scoop ice cream parlor. Mayor Daniel Lurie named it among businesses preparing to open under the grant program in an August 12, 2026 press release. No opening date has been announced.

restaurants.name: Old Skool Cafe

restaurants.name: Ocean Ale House

restaurants.name: Pho Golden
restaurants.description: A casual Excelsior Vietnamese restaurant well-regarded for its pho and dishes featuring grilled pork.

restaurants.name: Calabria Brothers
restaurants.description: An Excelsior Italian deli counter known for oversized, generously filled sandwiches made to order.

restaurants.name: Restaurante Familiar
restaurants.description: An Excelsior neighborhood staple serving Salvadoran and Mexican fare with praised entrees at family-friendly prices.

restaurants.name: Los Planes de Renderos
restaurants.description: A popular Excelsior Salvadoran spot focused on pupusas and traditional Central American comfort food.

restaurants.name: Don Chuy's
restaurants.description: A beloved Excelsior corner store recognized for its outstanding carnitas burrito.

restaurants.name: 7 Mile House
restaurants.description: A Visitacion Valley landmark at Bayshore Boulevard and Geneva Avenue, one of San Francisco's oldest continuously operating bars, still serving drinks on the same corner for generations.

restaurants.name: Pakwan

shops.name: Meizzei Hardware

shops.name: Ocean Subs
shops.description: An Excelsior lunch staple praised for its Original Sub on toasted Dutch crunch, stacked with Italian meats and a tangy herb vinaigrette.

artEntertainment.name: Ruth Williams Opera House (Bayview Opera House)
artEntertainment.type: Historic performing arts and cultural center
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest extant theater and Landmark #8, the Ruth Williams Opera House is the cultural anchor of Bayview–Hunters Point, hosting concerts, theater, Stoop Sessions, community events, and youth arts programs.

artEntertainment.name: Jerry Garcia Amphitheater

gymsRecreation.name: India Basin Shoreline Park
gymsRecreation.description: A newly developed waterfront park on the Bayview shore offering San Francisco Bay views, restored native habitat, and public shoreline access.
